A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MPVA research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original causal-fairness estimation and classification experiments on semi-synthetic D1/D2 and Credit/German datasets, including a layer-sensitivity analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds baseline results, a data-generation perturbation study, and runtime and memory measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions train an MPNN/MLP, freeze its parameters while training a cVAE, generate outcomes under global sensitive-attribute interventions, and regularize classification using causal disparity. v2's shared-component formulation explains the retained procedure rather than introducing a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Credit-based D1/D2 and the Credit/German classification tasks remain. Section 6.4.2 adds a perturbed D2 scenario with multiplicative interactions between A and UX, extending evaluation beyond the original data-generation conditions without adding a new dataset or prediction task.

E2.justification: v2 Table 4 adds evaluated NIFTY and FairINV rows to the Credit/German comparison while retaining every original comparator. These methods also participate in the new computational-cost comparison. The semi-synthetic comparison methods remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include perturbation strengths 0, 0.5, and 1 with absolute estimated-versus-true gCF error, and Credit runtime/memory evaluation with a reported 3600-second timeout for GEAR. Existing fairness metrics and stated training budgets remain unchanged; expanded dataset descriptions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused sensitivity test of estimation error under perturbed data generation and computational-cost profiling in Appendix C.3. The original layer-sensitivity analysis is retained. Figure 4 consolidates previously displayed fairness–accuracy curves rather than establishing a new ablation.

E5.justification: v1 already reports five repeated executions and numerical plus/minus values. v2 explicitly identifies the summaries as means and standard deviations across five independent runs. This clarifies uncertainty reporting without establishing additional runs or new statistical tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and all original real-data result rows are numerically unchanged. Added outcomes include NIFTY/FairINV scores, perturbation-study error increasing from 0.0075 to 0.1142, and computational measurements such as MPVA's 29.2358 seconds and 1365 MB. These extend the evidence rather than demonstrate improved performance over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: v2 adds an explicit hedge-based nonidentifiability argument when Graph Independence fails, Proposition 3 with backdoor and positivity requirements, and Corollary 5 with an intervention-invariance assumption for the learned shared component. These substantially expand the formal identification and estimation treatment. The original interventional-distribution formula and appendix proof are retained, with renumbering and corrected cross-references.

C1.justification: The central claims about MPVA, interventional estimation, and fair classification remain. v2 explicitly frames its theoretical contribution as restoring mechanism invariance across heterogeneous neighborhoods, and its conclusion adds a claim of maintained performance under varying conditions. This refines the contribution framing without replacing the research objective.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands discussion of mechanism invariance, identification failure, and assumption applicability. Its new limitations section identifies reliance on a known causal graph, explicitly represented graph dependencies, and a single sensitive attribute. Appendix C.1 adds arguments that the datasets satisfy Graph Independence, while Appendix C.3 interprets resource measurements as evidence of scalability.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a public-repository pointer instead of v1's supplementary-zip reference, reports Credit's 30,000 instances, and expands feature-allocation and noise-generation descriptions. It removes v1's explicit sentence about synthetic-edge probabilities based on generated-feature similarity. The stated software, hardware, optimizer, learning rates, and epoch counts remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references covering FairINV, FairGT, fair graph U-Net, additional counterfactual-fairness work, and intersectional fairness, while removing Xu et al. (2019). The existing graph-interference and fairness literature discussion is largely retained; moving it from the appendix to Section 2 is primarily structural.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanation, experimental discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related Work moves into the main text, identification and estimation receive separate subsections, and the appendices are reordered. v2 also adds a dedicated limitations section, removes the ethics section, and changes the assumption terminology to conditions.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the MPVA overview, merges v1 Figures 1–3 into a multipanel Figure 1 with a new condition-violation diagram, and adds a consolidated trade-off display. It expands the real-data table, adds perturbation and computational-cost tables, relocates retained plots, and adopts a different journal layout.

improvement.justification: Explicit identification requirements, additional comparisons, clearer presentation, and substantive limitations improve transparency and assessability. However, important new validation claims remain insufficiently supported: the multiplicative A–UX interaction can still fit the stated internal mechanism and does not itself establish violation of UX–C independence, while separate feature subsets do not establish independence either. The revision offers useful improvements without conclusively resolving the causal-assumption concerns.
